subject: Discovery recap: SDK priorities, function-calling, streaming & rerank acceptance
messages:
From: Emily Barnes <emily@nimble-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Li <alex@nimble-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick recap from today's discovery

Jordan — thanks for carving out time today. Alex and I appreciated the walkthrough; a quick recap and a few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Primary pain: search and product discovery relevance for fast-moving retail catalog (100k SKUs) — we currently see stale recommendations and latency spikes during peak traffic.
2) Goals: reduce rerank latency to <150ms P99, stable token cost per query, and a clear migration path from our existing microservice to Redwood SDK with function-calling hooks (for product metadata lookups).
3) Integration concerns: we need streaming partial outputs for progressive UI updates, deterministic structured outputs to fit into our analytics schema, and a plan for embeddings refresh cadence for nightly product updates.

We attached a short MVP requirements doc and a one-page tech checklist. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended SDK changes for function-calling + streaming? Also curious about fallback options if the quantized variant yields quality regressions.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Barnes
Head of Product — Search & Discovery
Nimble Retail
[Attachment: nimble_mvp_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Barnes <emily@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Alex Li <alex@nimble-retail.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap from today's discovery

Emily — great meeting, thanks for the clear problem statement. Short answers and next steps below.

Summary answers:
- SDK + function-calling: Yes — Redwood SDK supports function/tool calling. For this use case we'll recommend adding a single function for product_metadata_lookup(product_id) that runs synchronously before generation, plus a secondary asynchronous sidecar for enrichment if needed.
- Streaming: SDK streaming is supported; it can emit partial chunks as tokens are generated and include structured deltas for UI stitching.
- Structured outputs: We recommend a two-phase prompt pattern and a strict JSON schema enforcement step in the SDK to minimize hallucinations.
- Embeddings/rerank: Nightly rebuilds are fine; we can surface a delta-only ingest to reduce re-embedding costs.

Immediate asks (from our side):
- Can you share the sample product metadata schema (IDs, attributes, category tree) so Ava can draft a function signature?
- Confirm expected QPS during peak (ballpark) so we size batching/caching and suggest Dedicated vs Hosted.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ava will produce an SDK patch (diff) with a function-calling example and streaming snippet — target Thu 16 Sep.
2) Jordan/Sergio to follow up with a short cost/throughput recommendation once we have peak QPS.
3) Quick sync on Fri if needed to walk the SDK example live.

I'll attach a draft SDK diff for context when Ava is ready. Thanks again — excited to help.

— Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.ai]

From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Emily Barnes <emily@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap from today's discovery

Emily / team — quick technical note and attached patch with the minimal SDK changes I think will get you unblocked. Highlights of the patch (redwood_sdk_delta.patch):

- Added product_metadata_lookup function pattern in SDK (sync)
- Streaming helper: emit_chunk(metadataDelta, tokenChunk) to make UI stitching deterministic
- Structured-output validator: JSON schema enforcement hook (optional strict mode)
- Embedding helper: delta-only upsert API with per-namespace TTL to support nightly refreshes

Caveats and quality considerations:
- Quantized model variant may reduce cost but could lower rerank precision on corner cases; I included a quick A/B test harness in the patch.
- For P99 latency targets we should enable KV prefix caching for common SKUs and set batch windows to 10–25ms; I'll include recommended values in the patch notes.

Attached the patch and a short example usage snippet. If you can share the product metadata sample (CSV or JSON), I'll adapt the function signature immediately.

Next step: Jordan — pinging you to confirm a Fri 10am PT demo with Emily/Alex to walk the patch and run a live rerank sample.

— Ava Chen
Senior Developer Advocate, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_sdk_delta.patch (diff)]

From: Emily Barnes <emily@nimble-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>, Alex Li <alex@nimble-retail.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap from today's discovery

Thanks Jordan and Ava — this is very helpful. Alex and I confirm the following: 

- We'll send a sanitized product sample by EOD (CSV with ~5k rows) so you can wire the product_metadata_lookup signature.
- Peak expected QPS: ~450 reads/sec (with 4× spikes during promotions).
- We're comfortable trying the quantized variant in a canary for lower-cost runs as long as we have fallback to full-precision if quality drops.

Fri 10am PT works for a short demo — please send a calendar invite. Also please include a short acceptance criteria checklist in the invite (latency thresholds, acceptable rerank precision lift, embedding staleness window).

Thanks — Emily
Emily Barnes
Head of Product — Search & Discovery
Nimble Retail
